document_metadata.document_title: NWFWMD Environmental Resource Permit Applicant’s Handbook Volume II (design standards)

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: NWFWMD ERP AH Vol II stormwater quality criteria (Parts II/IV/V) including retention system treatment volume and additional quality standards. Quantity/flood criteria include 10-year floodplain storage and 100-year floodway conveyance limits.
peak_flow_calculation_method: Stormwater quantity rate and volume controls (Part III)

evidence.excerpt: ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCE PERMIT APPLICANT’S HANDBOOK VOLUME II
Design Criteria and Guidelines for Retention Systems ... Treatment Volume
Stormwater Quantity: Rate and Volume Controls
Retention Systems; On-Line and Off-line Stormwater Systems
The retention system must provide the capacity for the appropriate treatment volume of stormwater specified in Section 5.2 of this Volume within 72 hours following a storm event
The system shall be designed to recover the required treatment volume of stormwater runoff within 72 hours following a storm event assuming average antecedent moisture conditions.
The exfiltration trench system shall be designed so that the invert elevation of the trench is at least two feet above the seasonal high ground water table elevation
The average length to width ratio of the pond must be at least 2:1.

extraction_quality.review_notes: Municipal map coverage via NWFWMD ERP AH Vol II. Canonical special_district record: fl-nwfwmd-erp-ah2. Capital coverage via NWFWMD ERP AH Vol II (regional design criteria). City operating-permit checklists not separately ingested.

design_parameters.enrich_notes: Treatment volume sizing references NWFWMD ERP Vol I Sections 8.3 and 9 (nutrient performance), not a fixed inch WQv depth in these excerpts. Retention and exfiltration share 72-hour recovery at average AMC; exfiltration optional safety factor includes 36-hour drawdown design. Wet detention requires half of treatment volume drawdown in 48–60 hours and minimum L:W 2:1; max pond depth 12 ft. Exfiltration trench invert minimum 2 ft above seasonal high groundwater (24 in). Swales sized for 3-year, 1-hour storm infiltration on HSG A/B; cross-section top width:depth ≥6:1. Appendix B-2 cites detention-with-filtration checklist (FDM 1988), not a standalone sand filter depth standard in Part V.
